title: Recipe scaling preserves ingredient ratios rather than absolute indexed doses
summary: A speculative functional hypothesis treats repeated recipe instructions as proportionally scalable: increasing the number of product units multiplies each ingredient share, while an absolute indexed prescription keeps fixed amounts.

design.unit: matched recipe records with an explicit product count and at least two ingredient amounts
design.contrast: ratio-preserving scaling versus fixed indexed amounts
design.prediction: When product count changes within the same recipe template, ingredient ratios should remain constant under the scaling model; the indexed model predicts stable absolute amounts and changing ratios.
design.countermodel: The same surface alternation could reflect editorial batch conventions, lexicalized forms, or analyst counting choices without either proposed semantic rule.
design.falsifier: A matched count change preserves absolute amounts while the source explicitly marks a scaled batch, or ratios vary without a batch/count change.
design.principal_risk: Independent product counts and ingredient amounts are unavailable. Near IDEA000049 quantity calibration and old recipe quantity families, but the contrast is transformation across batch size, not unit interpretation or conservation.
